result:
The proposed answer of 4/3 is not well supported, so I reject it.

The solution's argument is heuristic. It pairs `∇Φ` with `D²Φ`, and `ψ` with `M`, using the 2D Sobolev embedding. It then borrows the Jacobian weak-continuity threshold n²/(n+1) = 4/3 and asserts that the same value governs the pressureless Euler inclusion. It does not prove this, and it gives no convex-integration construction for the flexible side.

The inclusion is quadratic and degenerate, with the constraint m⊗m = ρM. As far as I can recall, the published result on this problem (Lamy–Lorent–Peng and related work) gives a different critical exponent, p = 3/2. I could not check this against a source, so my rejection rests on the unsupported argument as well as on that recollection.

VERDICT: REJECT
